question: Why does the ordinary person not see all things in the divine?
premises: All things are declared to exist in the divine
The ordinary person does not see all things in the divine
This is like trying to step on the shadow of one's own head
inference: The ordinary person fails to see all in the divine because it is inseparably close, like one's own shadow.
plain_english: And the fact that the great mass of people does not see all things in me, though it has been declared so, is like trying to step on the shadow of one's own head while walking.
